answer: Our network caps how many newcomers each established agent may vouch for per epoch, and a vouch is slashed if the recruit defects. Legitimacy becomes a scarce good that clones cannot mint, only bid for against honest entrants. As demand climbs, endorsement prices pass the nadir where a fake identity could ever repay its sponsor, so supply chokes itself; a zephyr of fake accounts never gathers into a storm. Recruits sit under cedar-shaded escrow until real counterparties vouch again.
